341|# =============================================================================
342|# Context Compression (Auto-shrinks long conversations)
343|# =============================================================================
344|# When conversation approaches model's context limit, middle turns are
345|# automatically summarized to free up space while preserving important context.
346|#
347|# HOW IT WORKS:
348|# 1. Tracks actual token usage from API responses (not estimates)
349|# 2. When prompt_tokens >= threshold% of model's context_length, triggers compression
350|# 3. Protects first 3 turns (system prompt, initial request, first response)
351|# 4. Protects last N turns (default 20 messages = ~10 full turns of recent context)
352|# 5. Summarizes middle turns using a fast/cheap model
353|# 6. Inserts summary as a user message, continues conversation seamlessly
354|#
355|# Post-compression tail budget is target_ratio × threshold × context_length:
356|#   200K context, threshold 0.50, ratio 0.20 → 20K tokens of recent tail preserved
357|#   1M   context, threshold 0.50, ratio 0.20 → 100K tokens of recent tail preserved
358|#
359|compression:
360|  # Enable automatic context compression (default: true)
361|  # Set to false if you prefer to manage context manually or want errors on overflow
362|  enabled: true
363|
364|  # Fail closed before lossy compaction unless an active memory provider that
365|  # implements the pre-compress checkpoint contract (API v2) confirms its
366|  # durable checkpoint (default: false). With this on and no checkpoint, the
367|  # compaction attempt errors with BLOCKED_MISSING_PREREQUISITE and the
368|  # uncompressed transcript is preserved for a later retry. The gate binds to
369|  # every compaction authority: server-side native compaction
370|  # (codex_responses_native) is suppressed while armed, post-turn
371|  # micro-compaction is forced off (no checkpoint hook in its path), and the
372|  # codex_app_server API mode is refused at agent init (the codex agent
373|  # compacts its own thread — no checkpoint can be guaranteed there). Only
374|  # enable it with a checkpoint-capable provider configured — see
375|  # website/docs/developer-guide/memory-provider-plugin.md
376|  # ("Pre-Compress Checkpoints").
377|  checkpoint_required: false
378|
379|  # Opt-in compression progress notices on chat platforms (default: false).
380|  # By design, routine automatic compression is SILENT on human-facing chat
381|  # gateways (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ...) — it happens in the background
382|  # with server-side logging only. Set true to also deliver the routine
383|  # progress statuses (compacting started, preflight/pre-API compression,
384|  # idle compaction, retry progress, and the compaction-complete notice) to
385|  # chat platforms. Unrelated operational noise (auxiliary model failures,
386|  # provider retry chatter) stays suppressed either way, and compression
387|  # FAILURE notices + manual /compress feedback are always visible
388|  # regardless of this setting. (#52995)
389|  progress_notices: false
390|
391|  # Trigger compression at this % of model's context limit (default: 0.50 = 50%)
392|  # Lower values = more aggressive compression, higher values = compress later
393|  # Models with context windows below 512K are floored at 0.75 (raise-only) so
394|  # compaction doesn't fire with half the window still free; set above 0.75 to override.
395|  threshold: 0.50
396|
397|  # Per-model threshold overrides: keys are substring-matched against the model
398|  # name (longest match wins). Useful when some models need different compaction
399|  # points — e.g. a 1M-context model can compress later (0.30) while a 128K
400|  # model needs to compress earlier (0.60). The small-context floor (75% for
401|  # <512K models) still applies on top of per-model overrides.
402|  # model_thresholds:
403|  #   "glm-5.2": 0.40
404|  #   "claude-sonnet": 0.35
405|  #   "gpt-5": 0.30
406|
407|  # Absolute token cap for the compression trigger (default: 256000).
408|  # Compression fires at the LOWER of the ratio-based threshold and this count,
409|  # bounding large-window sessions while lower proportional triggers still win
410|  # whenever they fall below the cap. The cap survives model switches and fallbacks.
411|  # Set null to restore ratio-only behavior.
412|  codex_gpt55_autoraise: true
413|
414|  # Fraction of the threshold to preserve as recent tail (default: 0.20 = 20%)
415|  # e.g. 20% of 50% threshold = 10% of total context kept as recent messages.
416|  # Summary output is separately capped at 12K tokens (Gemini output limit).
417|  # Range: 0.10 - 0.80
418|  target_ratio: 0.20
419|
420|  # Number of most-recent messages to always preserve (default: 20 ≈ 10 full turns)
421|  # Higher values keep more recent conversation intact at the cost of more aggressive
422|  # compression of older turns.
423|  protect_last_n: 20
424|
425|  # Minimum number of REAL (actionable) user messages guaranteed to survive in
426|  # the uncompressed tail (default: 1 = the existing single last-user anchor,
427|  # behavior-preserving). Raise to e.g. 3 to keep the last 3 real user turns
428|  # verbatim even when bulky tool outputs fill the tail token budget — blank
429|  # platform echoes, compaction handoffs, and synthetic continuation rows never
430|  # count toward N. The tail can exceed the token budget when this pulls the
431|  # cut back; the guarantee wins over the budget by design.
432|  min_tail_user_messages: 1
433|
434|  # Compression retry rounds before a turn gives up with "max compression
435|  # attempts reached" (default: 3, same as the previous hardcoded value).
436|  # Raise (e.g. 6) for tool-schema-heavy sessions where 3 rounds cannot bring
437|  # the request estimate under the threshold. Validated >= 1, hard cap 10.
438|  max_attempts: 3
439|
440|  # Codex app-server (codex CLI runtime) thread-compaction mode. The codex
441|  # agent owns the real thread context on this runtime, so Hermes' summarizer
442|  # cannot shrink it — compaction goes through the app server instead.
443|  #   native = let Codex decide when to compact its own thread (default)
444|  #   hermes = let Hermes threshold trigger Codex thread/compact/start
445|  #   off    = Hermes will not auto-trigger compaction; Codex may still compact natively
446|  codex_app_server_auto: native
447|
448|  # Native OpenAI Responses server-side compaction (default: false). When true,
449|  # gpt-5.6-family models on the DIRECT OpenAI API (api.openai.com) or a ChatGPT
450|  # Codex subscription, plus exact gpt-6-astra on official Codex OAuth, compact
451|  # server-side: OpenAI prunes older context into an
452|  # encrypted checkpoint that Hermes replays on later turns. No other provider,
453|  # route, or model is affected. Hermes' local compression stays armed as the
454|  # fallback and still handles every non-eligible session.
455|  codex_responses_native: false
456|
457|  # Optional absolute server compaction trigger in input tokens. The default
458|  # null value follows the resolved local compression trigger with an 8192 token
459|  # safety margin. For example, a local trigger of 765000 selects 756808.
460|  # A positive integer stays absolute and only clamps downward when needed so
461|  # the server compacts first. Invalid values use this automatic behavior. If
462|  # the local trigger is unavailable, automatic mode uses 200000.
463|  codex_responses_compact_threshold:
464|
465|  # Number of non-system messages to protect at the head of the transcript, in
466|  # ADDITION to the system prompt (which is always implicitly protected).
467|  # Head messages are NEVER summarized — they survive every compression
468|  # indefinitely. This gives stable early context for short/medium sessions,
469|  # but in long-running sessions that rely on rolling compaction the pinned
470|  # opening turns may not match how you want the session framed over time.
471|  # Set to 0 to preserve ONLY the system prompt (plus the rolling summary
472|  # and recent tail) — the cleanest configuration for long-running sessions.
473|  # Default 3 preserves the system prompt plus the first three non-system
474|  # head messages, matching the pre-feature behaviour.
475|  protect_first_n: 3
476|
477|  # Idle compaction (default: 0 = disabled). When > 0, a session that resumes
478|  # after at least this many seconds of inactivity compacts its accumulated
479|  # history up front, before the first reply, so a long-lived thread you come
480|  # back to later doesn't re-read its full stale context on every turn.
481|  # Time-based, so it complements (does not replace) the size-based `threshold`
482|  # above. It is skipped when the context is already small (at or below the
483|  # post-compression target = threshold × target_ratio), so it never wastes a
484|  # summarization on a short idle thread. Example: 1800 = compact after 30 min idle.
485|  idle_compact_after_seconds: 0
486|
487|  # Gateway session-hygiene turn-hold budget (default: 10). Max seconds an
488|  # arriving user turn is held while a still-streaming hygiene summary
489|  # finishes. Distinct from hygiene_timeout_seconds (compressor inactivity
490|  # budget): this bounds user-visible latency so chat transports (Telegram
491|  # ~30s) do not drop a silent connection. On expiry the turn proceeds
492|  # uncompressed; the detached worker keeps its commit admission (when the
493|  # commit is watermark-fenced) and the summary is adopted at the next safe
494|  # boundary. Thinking-model summarizers often need longer than 10s to emit
495|  # the first content token — raise to 300 (or >= your summarizer's real
496|  # time-to-first-content) only if you want THIS turn to wait for the
497|  # compression instead of adopting it one turn late.
498|  hygiene_max_turn_hold_seconds: 10
499|
500|  # Proactive tool-result prune (default: 0 = disabled). Opt-in token trigger
501|  # for a deterministic, no-LLM prune of OLD tool-result payloads, run
502|  # independently of `threshold` above. On large-window models (512K/1M) the
503|  # ratio threshold rarely fires, so bulky tool outputs (terminal dumps, file
504|  # reads, web extracts) ride along in history and get re-billed every turn.
505|  # When re-sent history exceeds this many tokens, the prune dedupes identical
506|  # results, summarizes older oversized ones, and truncates large tool-call
507|  # arguments — protecting the most recent `protect_last_n` messages and never
508|  # calling the model. Try 48000 to enable. Built-in compressor engine only;
509|  # other context engines inherit a safe no-op.
510|  # NOTE: a committed prune rewrites already-sent history, which invalidates
511|  # the provider's prompt-cache prefix — the min_reclaim gate below keeps
512|  # those cache breaks episodic (like a compression boundary) instead of
513|  # per-turn.
514|  proactive_prune_tokens: [REDACTED_SECRET]  # The prune's summarize pass only touches tool results larger than this many
517|  # characters (clamped to >= 200 so a generated summary can't be
518|  # re-summarized). Default 8000.
519|  proactive_prune_min_result_chars: 8000
520|
521|  # A proactive prune only COMMITS when it reclaims at least this many tokens
522|  # (measured on the pruned output). This is the prompt-cache hysteresis gate:
523|  # one meaningful, amortized cache break per batch of stale tool output
524|  # instead of a tiny break on every tool iteration. 0 = commit any non-zero
525|  # prune. Default 4096.
526|  proactive_prune_min_reclaim_tokens: [REDACTED_SECRET]  # To pin a specific model/provider for compression summaries, use the
529|  # auxiliary section below (auxiliary.compression.provider / model).
530|
531|# =============================================================================
532|# Tool-result budget (optional)
533|# =============================================================================
534|# Controls when a large tool result is spilled to disk (full output saved to
535|# $HERMES_HOME/cache/spillover, preview + path kept in context). MCP tool
536|# results (tools named mcp_*) spill at a tighter 50,000-char threshold than
537|# the generic 100K default: MCP servers routinely return un-paginated 20-50K
538|# payloads that bloat context and slow every subsequent turn. Nothing is
539|# lost — the full result is on disk and readable with read_file.
540|#
541|# tool_budget:
542|#   mcp_result_size_chars: 50000   # per-result spillover threshold for mcp_* tools

554|# =============================================================================
555|# Auxiliary Models (Advanced — Experimental)
556|# =============================================================================
557|# Hermes uses lightweight "auxiliary" models for side tasks: image analysis,
558|# browser screenshot analysis, web page summarization, TTS audio-tag insertion,
559|# and context compression.
560|#
561|# By default these use Gemini Flash via OpenRouter or Nous Portal and are
562|# auto-detected from your credentials.  You do NOT need to change anything
563|# here for normal usage.
564|#
565|# WARNING: Overriding these with providers other than OpenRouter or Nous Portal
566|# is EXPERIMENTAL and may not work.  Not all models/providers support vision,
567|# produce usable summaries, or accept the same API format.  Change at your own
568|# risk — if things break, reset to "auto" / empty values.
569|#
570|# Each task has its own provider + model pair so you can mix providers.
571|# For example: OpenRouter for vision (needs multimodal), but your main
572|# local endpoint for compression (just needs text).
573|#
574|# Provider options:
575|#   "auto"       - Best available: OpenRouter → Nous Portal → main endpoint (default)
576|#   "openrouter" - Force OpenRouter (requires OPENROUTER_API_KEY)
577|#   "nous"       - Force Nous Portal (requires: hermes auth add nous)
578|#   "gemini"      - Force Google AI Studio direct (requires: GOOGLE_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY)
579|#   "ollama-cloud" - Ollama Cloud (requires: OLLAMA_API_KEY)
580|#   "codex"       - Force Codex OAuth (requires: hermes model → Codex).
581|#                  Uses gpt-5.3-codex which supports vision.
582|#   "main"       - Use your custom endpoint (OPENAI_BASE_URL + OPENAI_API_KEY).
583|#                  Works with OpenAI API, local models, or any OpenAI-compatible
584|#                  endpoint.  Also falls back to Codex OAuth and API-key providers.
585|#
586|# Model: leave empty to use the provider's default.  When empty, OpenRouter
587|# uses "google/gemini-3-flash-preview" and Nous uses "gemini-3-flash".
588|# Other providers pick a sensible default automatically.
589|#
590|# Native vision embeds (vision_analyze / browser screenshots when the MAIN model
591|# is vision-capable) ride conversation history and are re-sent on every later
592|# API call, so both knobs below bound recurring cost:
593|#
594|# vision:
595|#   # Byte budget for one embedded image (clamped 64 KiB..4 MiB). Raise it for
596|#   # dense phone screenshots of tables that read as "unreadable" at 256 KB.
597|#   embed_target_bytes: 262144
598|#   # How often vision_analyze may embed the SAME image (region crops included)
599|#   # per session. Unset = 3 inside delegated subagents, unlimited for the main
600|#   # agent; a number applies everywhere; 0 = unlimited.
601|#   max_calls_per_image: 3
602|#
603|# auxiliary:
604|#   # Image analysis: vision_analyze tool + browser screenshots
605|#   vision:
606|#     provider: "auto"
607|#     model: ""              # e.g. "google/gemini-2.5-flash", "openai/gpt-4o"
608|#     timeout: 30            # LLM API call timeout (seconds)
609|#     download_timeout: 30   # Image HTTP download timeout (seconds)
610|#                            # Increase for slow connections or self-hosted image servers
611|#     reasoning_effort: ""   # Per-task thinking level: none, minimal, low, medium,
612|#                            # high, xhigh, max, ultra. Empty = provider default.
613|#                            # Works on every auxiliary task block (vision,
614|#                            # web_extract, compression, title_generation, curator,
615|#                            # background_review, moa_reference, ...). Example: run
616|#                            # compression at "low" and vision at "none" to cut
617|#                            # side-task latency/cost on reasoning models.
618|#
619|#   # Web page scraping / summarization + browser page text extraction
620|#   web_extract:
621|#     provider: "auto"
622|#     model: ""
623|#     reasoning_effort: "low"
624|#
625|#   # Gemini 3.1 TTS hidden audio-tag insertion
626|#   tts_audio_tags:
627|#     provider: "auto"       # empty model = your main chat model
628|#     model: ""
629|#     timeout: 30
630|#
631|#   # Automatic session title generation after the first exchange
632|#   title_generation:
633|#     enabled: true          # set false to disable auto-title generation
634|#     model_upgrade_enabled: true  # set false to keep the instant derived title and skip the model call
635|#     provider: "auto"
636|#     model: ""
637|#     timeout: 30
638|#     language: ""           # empty = match the user's language; or e.g. "English"
639|#
640|#   # Session search — summarizes matching past sessions
641|#   session_search:
642|#     provider: "auto"
643|#     model: ""
644|#     timeout: 30
645|#     max_concurrency: 3    # Limit parallel summaries to reduce request-burst 429s
646|#     extra_body: {}        # Provider-specific OpenAI-compatible request fields
647|#                           # Example for providers that support request-body
648|#                           # reasoning controls:
649|#                           # extra_body:
650|#                           #   enable_thinking: false
651|#                           # Some vLLM/Qwen deployments expect this nested:
652|#                           # extra_body:
653|#                           #   chat_template_kwargs:
654|#                           #     enable_thinking: false
655|#
656|#   # Auto-generated short session titles after the first exchange.
657|#   # Each active Discord/Telegram channel can spawn a background title
658|#   # call.  Cap concurrency to keep retries during provider incidents
659|#   # from amplifying the request burst.  Leave unset for legacy behavior
660|#   # (unlimited).
661|#   title_generation:
662|#     provider: "auto"
663|#     model: ""
664|#     # max_concurrency: 2    # Optional: cap simultaneous title calls
665|#
666|#   # Context compression — summarizes long sessions to shrink the prompt.
667|#   # Heavy and often hits the slowest provider chain.  Setting a small
668|#   # cap prevents many sessions from compressing simultaneously during
669|#   # provider degradation.  Leave unset for legacy behavior (unlimited).
670|#   compression:
671|#     provider: "auto"
672|#     model: ""
673|#     # max_concurrency: 2    # Optional: cap simultaneous compression calls
674|#     # no_progress_timeout: 60   # Codex/Responses-only: seconds a stream may go without a
675|#                                 # substantive event before it fails fast (default: 60).
676|#                                 # Independent of "timeout" above (the overall request
677|#                                 # budget) — raising "timeout" alone does not widen this
678|#                                 # window. Each substantive event re-arms it; a slow but
679|#                                 # progressing reasoning/summary stream is not affected.
680|#
681|#   # Post-turn memory/skill self-improvement review fork. Runs after a turn
682|#   # when the nudge intervals fire; writes skills/memories in a daemon thread.
683|#   # Usage is recorded under session_model_usage task='background_review'.
684|#   background_review:
685|#     enabled: true            # false = skip automatic forks (/refine still works)
686|#     provider: "auto"         # or pin a cheaper model (see memory.md)
687|#     model: ""
688|
689|# =============================================================================
690|# Persistent Memory
691|# =============================================================================
692|# Bounded curated memory injected into the system prompt every session.
693|# Two stores: MEMORY.md (agent's notes) and USER.md (user profile).
694|# Character limits keep the memory small and focused. The agent manages
695|# pruning -- when at the limit, it must consolidate or replace entries.
696|# Disabled by default in batch_runner.
697|#
698|memory:
699|  # Agent's personal notes: environment facts, conventions, things learned
700|  memory_enabled: true
701|
702|  # User profile: preferences, communication style, expectations
703|  user_profile_enabled: true
704|
705|  # Character limits (~2.75 chars per token, model-independent)
706|  memory_char_limit: 2200   # ~800 tokens
707|  user_char_limit: 1375     # ~500 tokens
708|
709|  # Periodic memory nudge: remind the agent to consider saving memories
710|  # every N user turns. Set to 0 to disable. Only active when memory is enabled.
711|  nudge_interval: 10        # Nudge every 10 user turns (0 = disabled)
712|
713|# =============================================================================
714|# Session Continuity (Messaging Platforms)
715|# =============================================================================
716|# Conversations persist across inactivity and daily boundaries. Use /new or
717|# /reset explicitly; context compression manages long conversations.
718|
719|# Maximum number of simultaneously active chat sessions across CLI, TUI,
720|# dashboard chat, and messaging gateway. Set to null, 0, or omit to allow
721|# unlimited concurrent sessions. When the limit is reached, new sessions get a
722|# clean error while existing active sessions keep their normal behavior. This
723|# top-level key takes precedence over gateway.max_concurrent_sessions. The cap
724|# is a best-effort single-host/profile runtime guard; Hermes fails open if the
725|# local runtime lease registry cannot be read or locked.
726|max_concurrent_sessions: 10
727|
728|# When true, group/channel chats use one session per participant when the platform
729|# provides a user ID. This is the secure default and prevents users in the same
730|# room from sharing context, interrupts, and token costs. Set false only if you
731|# explicitly want one shared "room brain" per group/channel.
732|group_sessions_per_user: true
733|
734|# =============================================================================
735|# Session Storage Retention (state.db)
736|# =============================================================================
737|# ~/.hermes/state.db keeps every session, message, and tool call, plus the
738|# FTS5 search indexes. Since #54189, auto-pruning is ON by default so the file
739|# stays bounded: at CLI/gateway/cron startup (at most once per
740|# min_interval_hours) Hermes deletes ENDED sessions whose last activity is
741|# older than retention_days. Open, pinned, and in-progress sessions are never
742|# deleted. Stale automation sessions (cron/kanban/subagent/one-shot CLI) whose
743|# process died without closing them are first *closed*, then aged through a
744|# further full retention window before removal.
745|#
746|# After a prune that removed rows, VACUUM reclaims disk space only when both
747|# the time throttle (min_vacuum_interval_days) has elapsed AND more than 25%
748|# of the file's pages are reclaimable — a dense database never pays for a full
749|# rewrite to reclaim a few MB.
750|#
751|# Uncomment to change the defaults shown; set auto_prune: false to keep every
752|# ended session forever (the pre-#54189 behavior).
753|# sessions:
754|#   auto_prune: true
755|#   retention_days: 90
756|#   vacuum_after_prune: true
757|#   min_vacuum_interval_days: 30
758|#   min_interval_hours: 24
759|
760|# Optional direct endpoint for autonomous Bot Mode rooms spanning gateways.
761|# Leave unset for the safe default: Desktop coordinates cross-gateway rooms and
762|# same-gateway rooms can still continue on their own. Set this only to the
763|# public HTTPS base URL that another trusted Hermes gateway can reach. The API
764|# server key authorizes the initial invitation; scoped grants are signed by a
765|# separate installation-private secret and survive API-key rotation. Disbanding
766|# a Group Chat revokes its known peer routes; API-key rotation alone does not.
767|# Network access should still be limited to the peer gateways (for example with
768|# your VPN or firewall).
769|# Plain HTTP is accepted only for loopback testing; every reachable peer URL
770|# must use HTTPS.
771|#
772|# gateway:
773|#   room_link_url: "https://hermes.example.net"
774|#
775|# The equivalent environment override is HERMES_ROOM_LINK_URL. After changing
776|# it, restart the gateway and reopen New Group Chat > Advanced; Hermes will
777|# re-check the selected gateways automatically.
778|
779|# Startup sweep of session rows orphaned by a dead gateway process.
780|# The normal disconnect cleanup runs on an in-process grace timer, so a
781|# gateway restart (update, crash, systemd) leaves those rows permanently
782|# "active". On every gateway boot — stdio TUI *and* the desktop/dashboard
783|# WS sidecar — tui/desktop/subagent rows whose start time AND newest
784|# message are both older than the session TTL (HERMES_TUI_SESSION_TTL_S,
785|# default 6h) are closed with end_reason "startup_orphan_reap".
786|# Messaging-platform sessions (Telegram, Discord, ...) are never touched;
787|# live in-memory sessions are excluded; swept sessions stay resumable.
788|#
789|# dashboard:
790|#   startup_orphan_sweep: true
791|
792|# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
793|# API Server — per-client model routing
794|# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
795|# Route different API clients to different models/providers on a single
796|# Hermes deployment.  Clients choose a backend by sending a specific string
797|# as the OpenAI ``model`` field.  Unmapped model values fall back to the
798|# global model configured in the ``model:`` section above, and an explicit
799|# session /model override always wins over a route.
800|#
801|# Configure via the ``platforms.api_server.extra.model_routes`` gateway
802|# config block:
803|#
804|#   platforms:
805|#     api_server:
806|#       enabled: true
807|#       extra:
808|#         key: "your-api-server-secret"
809|#         model_routes:
810|#           # Xiaozhi clients send model="minimax-m2" → routed to MiniMax via OpenRouter
811|#           minimax-m2:
812|#             model: "minimax/minimax-m1"
813|#             provider: "openrouter"          # optional — overrides global provider
814|#             # api_key: [REDACTED_SECRET]"sk-..."             # optional — per-route UPSTREAM provider
815|#             #                                 key (NOT caller auth; never logged)
816|#             # base_url: "https://..."       # optional — per-route base URL
817|#           # GPT clients keep their own alias
818|#           gpt-5:
819|#             model: "openai/gpt-5"
820|#             provider: "openrouter"
821|#
822|# Configured aliases are automatically listed by GET /v1/models so clients
823|# can discover them without manual coordination.  Caller authentication is
824|# unchanged: every request still authenticates with the global API server
825|# key (``extra.key`` / API_SERVER_KEY).
826|
827|# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
828|# Gateway Streaming
829|# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
830|# Stream tokens to messaging platforms in real-time. The bot sends a message
831|# on first token, then progressively edits it as more tokens arrive.
832|# Disabled by default — enable to try the streaming UX on Telegram/Discord/Slack.
833|# For Telegram, partial edits are sent as plain text and only the final edit uses MarkdownV2.
834|streaming:
835|  enabled: false
836|  # transport: edit           # "edit" = progressive editMessageText
837|  # edit_interval: 0.3        # seconds between message edits
838|  # buffer_threshold: 40      # chars before forcing an edit flush
839|  # cursor: " ▉"              # cursor shown during streaming
840|
841|# =============================================================================
842|# Skills Configuration
843|# =============================================================================
844|# Skills are reusable procedures the agent can load and follow. The agent can
845|# also create new skills after completing complex tasks.
846|#
847|skills:
848|  # Nudge the agent to create skills after complex tasks.
849|  # Every N tool-calling iterations, remind the model to consider saving a skill.
850|  # Set to 0 to disable.
851|  creation_nudge_interval: 15
852|
853|  # External skill directories — share skills across tools/agents without
854|  # copying them into ~/.hermes/skills/.  Each path is expanded (~ and ${VAR})
855|  # and resolved to an absolute path.  External dirs are read-only: skill
856|  # creation always writes to ~/.hermes/skills/.  Local skills take precedence
857|  # when names collide.
858|  # external_dirs:
859|  #   - ~/.agents/skills
860|  #   - /home/shared/team-skills
861|
862|# =============================================================================
863|# Agent Behavior
864|# =============================================================================
865|agent:
866|  # Maximum tool-calling iterations per conversation (default: 500)
867|  # Higher = more room for complex tasks, but costs more tokens
868|  # Recommended: 20-30 for focused tasks, 50-100 for open exploration
869|  max_turns: 500
870|
871|  # Inactivity timeout for gateway agent runs (seconds, 0 = unlimited).
872|  # The agent can run indefinitely when actively calling tools or receiving
873|  # API responses.  Only fires after the agent has been idle for this duration.
874|  # gateway_timeout: 1800
875|
876|  # Maximum time an alias routing key waits for an active turn holding the same
877|  # resolved session lease. On expiry Hermes rejects this inbound message and
878|  # asks the user to resend rather than running it without serialization.
879|  # Non-positive values fall back to the 5-second default.
880|  # gateway_turn_lease_timeout: 5
881|
882|  # Staged warning: send a warning before escalating to full timeout.
883|  # Fires once per run when inactivity reaches this threshold (seconds).
884|  # Set to 0 to disable the warning.
885|  # gateway_timeout_warning: 900
886|
887|  # Session stall watchdog (seconds). When a busy session has a pending
888|  # inbound follow-up and the agent activity clock is idle this long, the
889|  # gateway logs a WARNING and notifies the user to try /new. Does not kill
890|  # the turn (see gateway_timeout). 0 = disable. Default 300.
891|  # session_stall_timeout: 300
892|
893|  # Transcript-sanitiser repeated-heal escalation (#96870). The pre-send
894|  # sanitiser silently repairs empty non-final turns on the wire copy; after
895|  # this many heal passes within a 10-minute session window Hermes logs one
896|  # ERROR (with session id + heal pattern) and sends a ONE-TIME out-of-band
897|  # notice to the user suggesting /debug share or `hermes doctor`. The notice
898|  # goes through the status channel only — conversation context and prompt
899|  # caching are untouched. Set 0 to disable escalation (per-window WARNINGs
900|  # still fire). Default 3.
901|  # sanitizer_heal_escalation_threshold: 3
902|
903|  # Related in-agent compression timeouts (they live under the top-level
904|  # compression: block, shown here for discoverability next to the stall
905|  # watchdog they complement — a hung compression is a common stall cause):
906|  # compression:
907|  #   context_timeout_seconds: 120          # inactivity budget for in-agent
908|  #                                         # compress_context (0 = disable)
909|  #   context_total_ceiling_seconds: 600    # absolute cap on the pre-commit
910|  #                                         # wait even while tokens stream
911|
912|  # Graceful drain timeout for gateway stop/restart (seconds).
913|  # Default 0 = no drain: a restart interrupts in-flight agents immediately,
914|  # cleans up, and exits. Set a positive value only if you want a grace
915|  # window on /restart, and keep it well under systemd's TimeoutStopSec.
916|  # restart_drain_timeout: 0
917|
918|  # Cron-only floor under the same drain (seconds). Default 30.
919|  # restart_drain_timeout above is written for chat turns, which are cheap to
920|  # interrupt: the user is told the gateway is restarting and the session
921|  # resumes on their next message. A cron run has no such safety net — it is
922|  # recorded in jobs.json as a permanent failure, nobody is waiting on it, and
923|  # a recurring job simply skips to its next schedule. So in-flight cron work
924|  # gets its own grace window instead of inheriting the 0 above.
925|  # Clamped at runtime to the shutdown-watchdog leash (restart_drain_timeout
926|  # + 60s) minus teardown headroom, so values past ~50s need a matching
927|  # TimeoutStopSec bump to take effect. Set 0 to opt out and drain cron on
928|  # restart_drain_timeout like before.
929|  # cron_drain_timeout: 30
930|
931|  # In-band restart wait (seconds) for active turns to finish BEFORE stop()
932|  # begins. /restart and SIGUSR1 refuse new work, then wait up to this cap for
933|  # in-flight agent, cron and API runs to complete so the requesting turn is
934|  # not cut off by restart_drain_timeout. 0 = enter stop()/drain immediately.
935|  # The default (30 min) is a safety valve for wedged agents, not a target
936|  # latency; raise it for long unattended turns. Env: HERMES_RESTART_AFTER_TURN_TIMEOUT.
937|  # restart_after_turn_timeout: 1800
938|
939|  # Upper bound (seconds) a submitted prompt waits for the deferred agent
940|  # build (MCP discovery, model metadata, skills scan) before failing with a
941|  # visible error. The wait is patient — the message is delivered as soon as
942|  # the build completes, and a progress notice is shown past 30s — so this cap
943|  # only fires on a genuinely hung build. Raise it for deployments with many
944|  # slow or unreachable MCP servers. Default 600.
945|  # build_wait_timeout: 600
946|
947|  # Max app-level retry attempts for API errors (connection drops, provider
948|  # timeouts, 5xx, etc.) before the agent surfaces the failure. Lower this
949|  # to 1 if you use fallback providers and want fast failover on flaky
950|  # primaries (default 3). The OpenAI SDK does its own low-level retries
951|  # underneath this wrapper — this is the Hermes-level loop.
952|  # api_max_retries: 3
953|
954|  # Once api_max_retries AND the fallback chain are spent on a transient outage
955|  # (5xx, overloaded/529, connect/read timeouts) and nothing has been delivered
956|  # yet, Hermes waits and retries this many more cycles (jittered 15/30/60/60/60s;
957|  # a provider Retry-After wins, up to 120s) showing "Provider temporarily
958|  # unavailable — retrying automatically in Ns (cycle k/5); press Esc to stop"
959|  # instead of ending the turn. Auth/format/billing/policy errors never enter.
960|  # Set 0 to disable (default 5).
961|  # auto_recovery_cycles: 5
962|
963|  # After the agent edits code without fresh passing verification, nudge it to
964|  # verify before finishing. Off by default (false). Set true to force it on
965|  # everywhere, or "auto" for the surface-aware mode: on for interactive
966|  # coding surfaces (CLI, TUI, desktop) and programmatic callers, off on
967|  # conversational messaging surfaces (Telegram, Discord, etc.) where the
968|  # verification summary would reach a human as chat noise. The
969|  # HERMES_VERIFY_ON_STOP env var (1/0) takes precedence.
970|  # verify_on_stop: false
971|
972|  # Standing operator instructions for the coding posture (when Hermes is in a
973|  # code workspace). Appended to the coding brief as an extra system block, so
974|  # you can pin project-wide workflow rules without editing the shipped brief.
975|  # Accepts a string or a list of strings. Takes effect next session.
976|  # coding_instructions:
977|  #   - "For UI work, don't run tsc/lint until I approve the look."
978|  #   - "Clean the diff before you commit and push."
979|
980|  # When verify-on-stop finds edited code without fresh verification evidence,
981|  # append guidance for creative UI work (avoid broad tsc/lint/test before visual
982|  # approval) and clean-diff expectations. Set false to keep that nudge terse.
983|  # verify_guidance: true
984|
985|  # A `pre_verify` hook (plugin or shell, see Event Hooks docs) can keep the
986|  # agent going one more turn to verify/clean before finishing. This caps how
987|  # many times one turn may be nudged to continue, so a hook can't trap the loop.
988|  # Default 3.
989|  # max_verify_nudges: 3
990|
991|  # Enable verbose logging
992|  verbose: false
993|
994|  # Reasoning effort level (OpenRouter and Nous Portal)
995|  # Controls how much "thinking" the model does before responding.
996|  # Options: "xhigh" (max), "high", "medium", "low", "minimal", "none" (disable)
997|  # Providers with bespoke thinking tiers (a relay serving fast/thinking): use the
998|  # dict form and the level is sent verbatim. Bare strings stay strict (typo guard).
999|  #   reasoning_effort:
1000|  #     enabled: true
1001|  #     effort: thinking
1002|  reasoning_effort: "medium"
1003|
1004|  # Per-model reasoning effort overrides (optional dict)
1005|  # Key: any sensible model spelling works (exact, dots↔dashes interchangeable,
1006|  #      provider prefix optional). First match wins.
1007|  # Value: reasoning effort level (same options as reasoning_effort, dict form included)
1008|  # Override the global reasoning_effort for that specific model.
1009|  # NOTE: no `hermes config set` support for this key -- edit YAML directly.
1010|  # reasoning_overrides:
1011|  #   "openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.5": "xhigh"
1012|  #   "openai/gpt-5": "low"
1013|  #   "claude-opus-4.6": "high"           # bare model name also works
1014|  #   "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro": "xhigh" # dots and dashes are interchangeable
1015|
1016|  # Fast mode (OpenAI Priority Processing / xAI Grok 4.6 / Anthropic Fast Mode
1017|  # on Opus 4.8+). Premium pricing; only sent to first-party endpoints.
1018|  #   "" / "normal" - off (default)
1019|  #   "fast"        - every request
1020|  #   "auto"        - only the first fast_auto_seconds of every turn
1021|  #   "cold"        - that window on the first turn of a session only
1022|  # Also: /fast normal|fast|auto|cold [--global]
1023|  service_tier: ""
1024|  fast_auto_seconds: 60
1025|
1026|  # Custom personalities (use with /personality command).
1027|  # Built-ins (helpful, concise, technical, creative, teacher, kawaii, catgirl,
1028|  # pirate, shakespeare, surfer, noir, uwu, philosopher, hype) are always
1029|  # available on every surface — defined once in hermes_cli/personality.py.
1030|  # Entries here ADD new personalities or OVERRIDE a built-in by name.
1031|  # The active selection is stored in display.personality (never here, and
1032|  # never in agent.system_prompt — that field is your manual system prompt).
1033|  personalities: {}
1034|  #   mentor: "You are a supportive mentor. Guide, don't lecture."
1035|  #   reviewer:
1036|  #     system_prompt: "You are a meticulous code reviewer."
1037|  #     tone: "direct"
1038|  #     style: "terse"

1045|  delivery_ledger: true

1050|  loop_watchdog_max_strikes: 3

1281|# =============================================================================
1282|# MCP (Model Context Protocol) Servers
1283|# =============================================================================
1284|# Connect to external MCP servers to add tools from the MCP ecosystem.
1285|# Each server's tools are automatically discovered and registered.
1286|# See website/docs/user-guide/features/mcp.md for full documentation.
1287|#
1288|# Stdio servers (spawn a subprocess):
1289|#   command: the executable to run
1290|#   args: command-line arguments
1291|#   env: environment variables (only these + safe defaults passed to subprocess)
1292|#
1293|# HTTP servers (connect to a URL):
1294|#   url: the MCP server endpoint
1295|#   headers: HTTP headers (e.g., for authentication)
1296|#
1297|# Optional per-server settings:
1298|#   timeout: tool call timeout in seconds (default: 120)
1299|#   connect_timeout: initial connection timeout (default: 60)
1300|#   keepalive_interval: liveness ping cadence in seconds (floored at 5s).
1301|#     HTTP servers default to 180s; lower it below the server's session TTL for
1302|#     servers that expire idle sessions quickly (e.g. Unreal Engine editor MCP,
1303|#     ~15s), otherwise idle tool calls hit an expired session and pay a slow
1304|#     reconnect. Stdio servers disable keepalive by default; set this explicitly
1305|#     to opt a stdio server in.
1306|#   lazy: register the server's tools from the on-disk schema cache at startup
1307|#     and only spawn/connect it on the first tool call (default: false). Saves
1308|#     one child process per server in processes that rarely call tools. Needs
1309|#     one prior live connect to populate the cache; a missing or stale cache
1310|#     entry falls back to the normal eager connect. The banner and the TUI show
1311|#     such a server as "lazy" with its cached tool count until it is first used.
1312|#
1313|# mcp_servers:
1314|#   time:
1315|#     command: uvx
1316|#     args: ["mcp-server-time"]
1317|#   filesystem:
1318|#     command: npx
1319|#     args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/home/user"]
1320|#   notion:
1321|#     url: https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
1322|#   github:
1323|#     command: npx
1324|#     args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
1325|#     env:
1326|#       GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN: [REDACTED_SECRET]"ghp_..."
1327|#
1328|# Sampling (server-initiated LLM requests) — enabled by default.
1329|# Per-server config under the 'sampling' key:
1330|#   analysis:
1331|#     command: npx
1332|#     args: ["-y", "analysis-server"]
1333|#     sampling:
1334|#       enabled: true           # default: true
1335|#       model: "gemini-3-flash" # override model (optional)
1336|#       max_tokens_cap: [REDACTED_SECRET]    # max tokens per request
1337|#       timeout: 30             # LLM call timeout (seconds)
1338|#       max_rpm: 10             # max requests per minute
1339|#       allowed_models: []      # model whitelist (empty = all)
1340|#       max_tool_rounds: 5      # tool loop limit (0 = disable)
1341|#       log_level: "info"       # audit verbosity
1342|
1343|# =============================================================================
1344|# Text-to-Speech
1345|# =============================================================================
1346|# TTS defaults to Edge TTS unless changed in ~/.hermes/config.yaml.
1347|# Gemini TTS supports persona/director prompt files, and Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS
1348|# can use a hidden auxiliary rewrite pass to insert expressive square-bracket
1349|# audio tags into the TTS script without showing tags in chat.
1350|#
1351|# tts:
1352|#   provider: "gemini"
1353|#   speed: 1.0              # global speed multiplier (provider-specific overrides this)
1354|#   # Per-platform audio upload limits. Built-in defaults: discord 10 MiB,
1355|#   # telegram 50 MiB, everything else 10 MiB, each with safety_ratio 0.85
1356|#   # (the fraction of max_file_bytes actually targeted). Override per platform:
1357|#   delivery_profiles:
1358|#     telegram:
1359|#       max_file_bytes: 52428800
1360|#       safety_ratio: 0.85
1361|#   gemini:
1362|#     model: "gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview"
1363|#     voice: "Kore"
1364|#     audio_tags: false
1365|#     persona_prompt_file: ""  # e.g. ~/.hermes/tts/radio-host.md
1366|#   xai:
1367|#     voice_id: "eve"       # built-in or custom voice ID from xAI Console
1368|#     language: "en"        # BCP-47 code ("en", "pt-BR") or "auto"
1369|#     speed: 1.0            # 0.7-1.5 playback speed
1370|#     auto_speech_tags: false  # insert expressive audio tags via LLM rewrite
1371|#     text_normalization: false  # normalize numbers/abbreviations/symbols
1372|#     optimize_streaming_latency: 0  # 0-2, trades quality for lower latency
1373|#     sample_rate: 24000    # 22050 / 24000 / 44100 / 48000
1374|#     bit_rate: 128000      # MP3 bitrate (codec=mp3 only)
1375|
1376|# =============================================================================
1377|# Voice Transcription (Speech-to-Text)
1378|# =============================================================================
1379|# Automatically transcribe voice messages on messaging platforms.
1380|# Providers: local (free, faster-whisper) | groq (free tier) | openai (Whisper API) | mistral (Voxtral Transcribe)
1381|# Set the corresponding API key in .env: GROQ_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, or MISTRAL_API_KEY.
1382|stt:
1383|  enabled: true
1384|  # provider: "local"          # auto-detected if omitted
1385|  # --- Cloud pre-upload silence trim (groq/openai/mistral/xai/elevenlabs/deepinfra) ---
1386|  # Local whisper gets Silero VAD; cloud endpoints otherwise receive raw audio —
1387|  # silence inflates upload time, per-audio-minute billing, and hallucination risk.
1388|  # Collapses pauses with ffmpeg client-side; clips under 12s skip the trim, and
1389|  # on any failure the original uploads untouched.
1390|  # cloud_trim_silence: true   # set false to always upload the original audio
1391|  # cloud_trim_threshold_db: -40  # audio quieter than this counts as silence
1392|  # cloud_trim_keep_ms: 300    # how much of each pause survives (keeps natural pacing)
1393|  # Optional static transcription prompt: vocabulary/context hints for
1394|  # prompt-capable backends. Composition is deterministic: this config value
1395|  # is the base, then `pre_transcription` hooks run in registration order with
1396|  # last-writer-wins semantics per field.
1397|  #
1398|  # Privacy: the final prompt is sent to the configured STT provider alongside
1399|  # the audio. Do not include secrets or session context you would not send to
1400|  # that provider.
1401|  #
1402|  # Length / truncation contract: Whisper-family backends (local, openai,
1403|  # groq, deepinfra) only use the final ~224 prompt tokens, so Hermes
1404|  # truncates longer prompts client-side (keeping the tail) with a WARNING
1405|  # log — never an error. Other backends own their own validation.
1406|  #
1407|  # Provider behavior:
1408|  #   local (faster-whisper)  -> `initial_prompt`, forwarded unchanged
1409|  #   openai / groq          -> `prompt`, forwarded unchanged
1410|  #   mistral                -> `prompt`, forwarded unchanged
1411|  #   deepinfra              -> OpenAI-compatible `prompt`, unchanged
1412|  #   local_command/xai/
1413|  #   elevenlabs             -> unsupported; DEBUG log, then continue
1414|  #   plugin providers       -> `prompt` in `**extra`; plugin owns limits
1415|  # prompt: "Hermes, Teknium, Nous Research, kanban"
1416|  local:
1417|    model: "base"              # tiny | base | small | medium | large-v3 | turbo
1418|    # language: ""             # auto-detect; set to "en", "es", "fr", etc. to force
1419|    # initial_prompt: ""       # Optional faster-whisper prompt, e.g. bias Chinese output to simplified Chinese
1420|    # --- Anti-hallucination hardening (whisper decodes junk from silence without these) ---
1421|    # vad: true                # Silero VAD filter (default on) — silence never reaches whisper.
1422|    #                          # Set false to restore raw behavior (e.g. transcribing music/ambient audio).
1423|    # vad_min_silence_ms: 500  # min silence (ms) that splits speech chunks when vad is on
1424|    # no_speech_prob_threshold: 0.6  # drop a segment only if no_speech_prob > this...
1425|    # logprob_threshold: -1.0       # ...AND avg_logprob < this (both must hit — quiet real speech survives)
1426|    # unload_after_idle_seconds: 0  # 0=never unload (default); e.g. 300 releases the model after 5min idle (frees VRAM on GPU; next voice message reloads it)
1427|  language: "en"               # GLOBAL language hint for every STT provider (per-provider language wins). Set "" for auto-detect.
1428|  # groq:
1429|  #   model: "whisper-large-v3-turbo"
1430|  #   language: ""             # blank = stt.language > HERMES_LOCAL_STT_LANGUAGE > auto-detect
1431|  openai:
1432|    model: "whisper-1"         # whisper-1 | gpt-4o-mini-transcribe | gpt-4o-transcribe | gpt-transcribe
1433|    language: ""               # auto-detect; set to "en", "es", "fr", etc. to force
1434|    timeout: 60                # request timeout in seconds; increase for self-hosted model cold starts
1435|    max_retries: 1             # OpenAI SDK transport retries; set 0 to disable
1436|  # mistral:
1437|  #   model: "voxtral-mini-latest"  # voxtral-mini-latest | voxtral-mini-2602
1438|  # deepinfra:
1439|  #   # Model id is discovered live from the DeepInfra catalog filtered
1440|  #   # by the `stt` surface tag — leave `model` blank to take the first
1441|  #   # live result. Pin only when you need a specific Whisper variant.
1442|  #   model: ""
1443|
1444|# Text-to-speech. Only the deepinfra block is documented here — the
1445|# remaining providers (edge, openai, xai, minimax, mistral, gemini,
1446|# elevenlabs, neutts, kittentts, piper) inherit sensible defaults from
1447|# DEFAULT_CONFIG in hermes_cli/config.py.
1448|# tts:
1449|#   provider: "deepinfra"
1450|#   deepinfra:
1451|#     # Model id is discovered live from the DeepInfra catalog filtered
1452|#     # by the `tts` surface tag — leave `model` blank to take the first
1453|#     # live result.
1454|#     model: ""
1455|#     voice: "default"
1456|
1457|# "Hey Hermes" hands-free wake word (off by default; toggle with /wake).
1458|# Full engine/provider options inherit from DEFAULT_CONFIG in
1459|# hermes_cli/config_defaults.py — only capture placement is documented here.
1460|# wake_word:
1461|#   enabled: false
1462|#   capture: "auto"    # auto | local | client
1463|#                      # auto: backend PortAudio mic when one exists; a remote
1464|#                      #       desktop on a mic-less (headless/VPS) backend
1465|#                      #       streams its own mic via the wake.feed RPC.
1466|#                      # local: always the backend mic (wake_word.input_device).
1467|#                      # client: always desktop-streamed PCM (detection stays
1468|#                      #         on the backend).
1469|
1470|# Image generation. Each provider plugin reads its own ``image_gen.<name>``
1471|# block; deepinfra discovers models live from
1472|# api.deepinfra.com/v1/openai/models filtered by the ``image-gen`` tag —
1473|# no model id is hardcoded, so retired models disappear automatically.
1474|# image_gen:
1475|#   provider: "deepinfra"

1489|# =============================================================================
1490|# Session Logging
1491|# =============================================================================
1492|# Session trajectories are automatically saved to logs/ directory.
1493|# Each session creates: logs/session_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_UUID.json
1494|#
1495|# The session ID is displayed in the welcome banner for easy reference.
1496|# Logs contain full conversation history in trajectory format:
1497|# - System prompt, user messages, assistant responses
1498|# - Tool calls with inputs/outputs
1499|# - Timestamps for debugging
1500|#
1501|# No configuration needed - logging is always enabled.
1502|# To disable, you would need to modify the source code.
1503|
1504|# =============================================================================
1505|# Code Execution Sandbox (Programmatic Tool Calling)
1506|# =============================================================================
1507|# The execute_code tool runs Python scripts that call Hermes tools via RPC.
1508|# Intermediate tool results stay out of the LLM's context window.
1509|code_execution:
1510|  timeout: 300         # Max seconds per script before kill (default: 300 = 5 min)
1511|  max_tool_calls: 50   # Max RPC tool calls per execution (default: 50)
1512|  # Local execution uses a persistent session kernel: variables, imports, and
1513|  # loaded data survive across execute_code calls in one conversation, so

## 5. Template rules being applied (and template bugs to fix)

From Shannon's Quadlet template:
- Networks: `frontend-net` (NPM only), `app-net` (proxied apps, outbound NAT), `db-net` (`--internal`), `infra-net` (admin/internal tools), all `--opt isolate=1`.
- Only NPM publishes ports. Apps have **no `PublishPort`**. NPM reaches apps by container name over `app-net`.
- Secrets go in `EnvironmentFile=/etc/podman/secrets/<svc>.env` (`chmod 600`, root-owned).
- Bind data under `/var/podman/<svc>/…`.
- `Restart=always`, `RestartSec=5`, `WantedBy=multi-user.target`, `AutoUpdate=registry` (NPM only in the template).

**Template bugs to correct in the new files (flag to Shannon):**
1. `Networks=frontend-net,app-net` is **not a valid Quadlet key**. Use one `Network=` line per network.
2. `HealthCheck=` is **not a valid Quadlet key**. Use `HealthCmd=` (+ `HealthInterval=` etc.).
3. `EnvironmentFile=/etc/podman/secrets/bookstack-db.env   # <-- …` has an inline comment, which systemd treats as part of the path. Put comments on their own line.
4. `--opt isolate=1` blocks traffic **between** networks, but containers on the **same** network still talk. So WebUI and agent must share a network (use `app-net`).

## 6. Target architecture

```
Internet ──443──> NPM (frontend-net + app-net)
                    ├─ hermes.shannonjlove.cloud      ──> hermes-webui:8787   (public; WebUI password + optional NPM auth)
                    └─ hermes-dash.shannonjlove.cloud ──> hermes-agent:9119   (access list 100.64.0.0/10 = Tailscale only)

app-net:  hermes-webui ──HERMES_API_URL=http://hermes-agent:8642──> hermes-agent
          (8642 gateway API and 8644 webhooks are never published)

Storage:  /var/podman/hermes/data   → agent:/opt/data (HERMES_HOME) and webui:/home/hermeswebui/.hermes
          hermes-agent-src (named volume) → agent:/opt/hermes, webui:/home/hermeswebui/.hermes/hermes-agent:ro
          /var/podman/hermes/workspace → webui:/workspace
UID/GID:  10000:10000 everywhere
```

Unified pattern (docs v0.14+): **one** `hermes-agent` process serves both the gateway and the dashboard, so `hermes-home` has a single writer. **Do not** run a separate `hermes-dashboard` container (it causes lock/`gateway_state.json` conflicts). The gateway ticks cron every 60 seconds, which fixes "Gateway not configured".

## 10. Risks / gotchas

- **Version pairing:** a mismatched WebUI/agent release pair breaks things in subtle ways. Pin both.
- **`API_SERVER_KEY` < 16 chars** means port 8642 never binds, and you get "Gateway endpoint not reachable".
- **UID mismatch** (1000 vs 10000) causes PermissionError on startup (docs troubleshooting #1).
- **Two writers to HERMES_HOME:** don't add a separate dashboard container.
- **`-desktop` image tag** may include GUI/browser bits; the server tag may differ. Verify browser-CDP tool support if Shannon uses browser tools.
- **Scale-to-zero:** the Nous instance was idle/"draining". Self-hosted, it runs 24/7, so check Nexus RAM/disk headroom.
- **Arch:** if D3 = sOs (ARM64), confirm the image has an arm64 manifest (`podman manifest inspect`).

## 6. DATA MIGRATION (Nous → LoveCloud)

### Step 1: Export from Nous instance
```bash
# On the Nous-hosted agent, ask Hermes to tar /opt/data (exclude cache/logs)
tar -czf /tmp/hermes-data-backup.tar.gz \
  --exclude=/opt/data/cache \
  --exclude=/opt/data/logs \
  /opt/data
# Result: ~5–10 MB depending on state.db size
```

**Method to get the tar to Nexus:** (Choose one)
- Have the Hermes agent itself push via rclone to `lovecloud-e2` / `idrive-e2`
- Use Nous portal SSH/export if available
- **NEVER paste `auth.json` contents into chat**

### Step 2: Stage on Nexus
```bash
mkdir -p /var/podman/hermes/{data,workspace}
tar -xzf /tmp/hermes-data-backup.tar.gz -C /var/podman/hermes/data --strip-components=1
chown -R 10000:10000 /var/podman/hermes/data
find /var/podman/hermes/data -type d -exec chmod 750 {} \;
find /var/podman/hermes/data -type f -exec chmod 640 {} \;
```

### Step 3: Config rewrite (critical)
Edit `/var/podman/hermes/data/config.yaml`:
- Replace `provider: nous` with `provider: openrouter` (or local Ollama if available)
- Pin model to OpenRouter `:free` models only (per governance)
- Remove or comment out `HERMES_DASHBOARD_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` (Nous-specific)
- Set `HERMES_SCALE_TO_ZERO: false` (self-host runs 24/7)
- Keep `cron.provider: chronos` (or remove if not used)

### Step 4: Re-auth expectations
- `/opt/data/auth.json` will have stale Nous Portal tokens; expect failures
- Replace with API keys from 1Password "LoveCloud LLM Runtime Access"
- Messaging credentials (Telegram, Discord, etc.) are blank; add if needed

### Step 5: Deploy & verify (see §7)

**Rollback:** `systemctl stop hermes-webui hermes-agent && rm -rf /var/podman/hermes`. Keep the Nous instance live until verification passes.

## 7. DEPLOY & VERIFICATION

### Pre-deploy checklist
```bash
# 1. Networks
podman network exists app-net || podman network create \
  --driver bridge --opt isolate=1 app-net

# 2. Directories + permissions
sudo mkdir -p /var/podman/hermes/{data,workspace} /etc/podman/secrets
sudo chown -R 10000:10000 /var/podman/hermes
sudo chown -R root:root /etc/podman/secrets
sudo chmod 700 /etc/podman/secrets

# 3. Check SELinux (if present)
getenforce  # returns "Permissive", "Enforcing", or "Disabled"
# If Enforcing, change Quadlet volumes from :Z to :z
```

### Place Quadlet files
```bash
sudo cp hermes-agent-src.volume hermes-agent.container hermes-webui.container \
  /etc/containers/systemd/
sudo cp hermes-agent.env hermes-webui.env /etc/podman/secrets/
sudo chmod 600 /etc/podman/secrets/*.env
```

### Validate + start
```bash
# Syntax check
/usr/libexec/podman/quadlet -dryrun -unit hermes-agent.container -unit hermes-webui.container

# Reload systemd
sudo systemctl daemon-reload

# Start agent first (wait for health)
sudo systemctl start hermes-agent
sleep 30
sudo systemctl status hermes-agent --no-pager

# Then start WebUI
sudo systemctl start hermes-webui
sleep 20
sudo systemctl status hermes-webui --no-pager
```

### Post-deploy verification
```bash
# [ ] Both containers healthy
podman healthcheck run hermes-agent
podman healthcheck run hermes-webui

# [ ] No published ports on Hermes containers (NPM only)
podman ps --format "{{.Names}} {{.Ports}}" | grep hermes

# [ ] Gateway API responds
podman exec hermes-webui curl -sS http://hermes-agent:8642/health/detailed

# [ ] WebUI can reach agent (check System Settings → Gateway status pill = green)
podman exec hermes-webui curl -sS http://hermes-agent:8642 -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_SERVER_KEY"

# [ ] Session history migrated (check browser; old conversations should appear)
# [ ] Approval card appears on guarded tool via browser chat
# [ ] Cron jobs tick on schedule (gateway ticks every 60s; check Tasks panel)
# [ ] Dashboard (hermes-dash.shannonjlove.cloud) only reachable over Tailscale
# [ ] No paid API keys active (check config.yaml + env files for REPLACE_WITH_)
```

## 8. COMMON ISSUES & FIXES

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| Gateway health check fails; `curl 127.0.0.1:8642` times out | `API_SERVER_KEY` missing or < 16 chars | Regenerate: `openssl rand -hex 24` |
| WebUI can't reach agent (`HERMES_API_URL=http://hermes-agent:8642` unreachable) | Network isolation or DNS | Check `podman network inspect app-net`; both containers must be on `app-net` |
| Permission denied on `/opt/data` files | UID mismatch (1000 vs 10000) | `chown -R 10000:10000 /var/podman/hermes/data` |
| `systemctl start hermes-webui` hangs (waits for agent) | Agent not healthy yet | Wait longer or check agent logs: `journalctl -u hermes-agent -f` |
| Dashboard (9119) reachable from public internet | NPM not enforcing Tailscale access list | Edit NPM host; set access list to `100.64.0.0/10` only |
| Old Nous-instance sessions don't appear | `state.db` not migrated or in wrong path | Check `/var/podman/hermes/data/state.db` exists and is readable by UID 10000 |
| Approval cards don't appear in browser chat | `HERMES_WEBUI_CHAT_BACKEND=gateway` not set or API key wrong | Verify both env files; check `HERMES_WEBUI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` = agent's `API_SERVER_KEY` |

**Date:** 2026-10-14

## 1. Current status

- `hermes-agent` and `hermes-webui` Quadlets appear to be deployed on **Nexus**, and the WebUI answers (from the iPhone Hermes WebUI app).
- **The WebUI cannot load the agent.** Exact error:

```
AIAgent not available -- check that hermes-agent is on sys.path
python: /app/venv/bin/python
HERMES_WEBUI_AGENT_DIR: (not set)
sys.path: (no entries mention hermes or agent)
Most common fix: install the agent in editable mode so its modules appear on sys.path:
  cd /path/to/hermes-agent && pip install -e .   then restart the WebUI.
Full troubleshooting: docs/troubleshooting.md ("AIAgent not available")
```

### Likely causes, in order
1. **`hermes-agent-src` volume is empty** in the WebUI. The WebUI started before the agent filled it, or the agent image keeps its source somewhere other than `/opt/hermes`, so the copy-on-first-mount never happened.
2. **`HERMES_WEBUI_AGENT_DIR` is not set**, so the WebUI doesn't look in `/home/hermeswebui/.hermes/hermes-agent`.
3. **The agent's Python dependencies are missing from `/app/venv`.** The WebUI may need to `pip install -e` the agent. The `:ro` mount in the v1.0 draft would block that, because an editable install writes build metadata into the source dir.

## 2. For Claude Code (run on Nexus as root)

### 2.1 Diagnose + safe fix
This is the same script Shannon got as a two-pass base64 one-liner. It's read-only except for adding the env var line and restarting the WebUI.

```bash
set -u;W=/etc/containers/systemd/hermes-webui.container
echo "== agent-src volume";M=$(podman volume inspect hermes-agent-src --format '{{.Mountpoint}}' 2>&1);echo "$M";ls -la "$M" 2>&1|head -15
R=$(find "$M" -maxdepth 3 -name run_agent.py 2>/dev/null|head -1);echo "run_agent.py: ${R:-NOT FOUND}"
echo "== agent /opt/hermes";podman exec hermes-agent sh -c 'ls /opt/hermes|head -15' 2>&1
echo "== webui mounts";podman inspect hermes-webui --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Destination}} <- {{.Source}} rw={{.RW}}{{println}}{{end}}' 2>&1
if [ -n "$R" ];then D=/home/hermeswebui/.hermes/hermes-agent${R#$M};D=${D%/run_agent.py};echo "AGENT_DIR=$D"
echo "== import test";podman exec hermes-webui /app/venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'$D');import run_agent;print('IMPORT OK')" 2>&1|tail -3
grep -q HERMES_WEBUI_AGENT_DIR $W||sed -i "/^ContainerName=hermes-webui/a Environment=HERMES_WEBUI_AGENT_DIR=$D" $W
systemctl daemon-reload;systemctl restart hermes-webui;sleep 20;fi
echo "== webui logs";journalctl -u hermes-webui -n 60 --no-pager|grep -iE 'agent|error|denied|read-only|install|sys.path'|tail -20
```

### 2.2 What to do with each result

| Result | Action |
|---|---|
| `run_agent.py: NOT FOUND` and `/opt/hermes` in the agent **has** source | Volume was never populated. `systemctl stop hermes-webui hermes-agent` → `podman volume rm hermes-agent-src` → `systemctl start hermes-agent` (copy-on-first-mount fills it) → wait for healthy → `systemctl start hermes-webui`. |
| `NOT FOUND` and `/opt/hermes` in the agent has **no** source | The agent image keeps its source elsewhere. Find it (`podman exec hermes-agent python -c "import run_agent,os;print(os.path.dirname(run_agent.__file__))"`), then remount the volume at that path in `hermes-agent.container`. |
| `IMPORT OK` | Env var was the fix. Confirm the app works. |
| Import fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: <some dependency>` | The WebUI venv needs the agent's deps. Read `docs/troubleshooting.md` ("AIAgent not available") in nesquena/hermes-webui and follow its container fix. **If it needs a writable mount, removing `:ro` from the agent-src mount is a change from the v1.0 plan. Ask Shannon first.** |
| Logs show "read-only file system" during install | Same as above: removing `:ro` needs Shannon's OK. |

Use `/usr/libexec/podman/quadlet -dryrun` after any Quadlet edit.

On this page

The web dashboard is a browser-based UI for managing your Hermes Agent installation. Instead of editing YAML files or running CLI commands, you can configure settings, manage API keys, and monitor sessions from a clean web interface.

tip

Hosted-mode auth uses Nous Portal OAuth; if you also want the dashboard to talk to a real backend, `hermes setup --portal` wires up the model and tool gateway too. See [Nous Portal](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/nous-portal).

## Quick Start [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#quick-start "Direct link to Quick Start")

```bash
hermes dashboard
```

This starts a local web server and opens `http://127.0.0.1:9119` in your browser. The dashboard runs entirely on your machine — no data leaves localhost.

### Options [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#options "Direct link to Options")

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--port` | `9119` | Port to run the web server on |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address |
| `--no-open` | — | Don't auto-open the browser |
| `--insecure` | off | **Deprecated / no-op.** Formerly bypassed auth on a non-loopback bind; it no longer disables authentication — a public bind always requires an auth provider (password or OAuth) |
| `--isolated` | off | When launched from a named profile (`worker dashboard`), run a dedicated per-profile server instead of routing to the machine dashboard |

```bash
# Custom port

hermes dashboard --port 8080

# Bind to all interfaces (use with caution on shared networks)

hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0

# Start without opening browser

hermes dashboard --no-open
```

## Managing multiple profiles [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#managing-multiple-profiles "Direct link to Managing multiple profiles")

The dashboard is a **machine-level** management surface: one server manages
every [profile](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/profiles) on the machine. A profile switcher in the
sidebar (visible whenever more than one profile exists) decides which
profile the management pages read and write — Config, API Keys, Skills,
MCP, Models, and the Chat tab all follow it. While a profile other than
the dashboard's own is selected, an amber banner names the managed profile
so the write target is never ambiguous.

The selection lives in the URL (`?profile=<name>`), so deep links like
`http://127.0.0.1:9119/skills?profile=worker` land with the switcher
preselected and survive refresh.

Launching the dashboard from a profile alias routes to the machine
dashboard instead of starting a second server:

```bash
worker dashboard

# → already running: opens the browser at ?profile=worker

# → not running:     starts the machine dashboard with "worker" preselected
```

A dashboard started this way keeps `worker` as its fallback scope for the
whole server lifetime: a deep link that omits `?profile=` (for example a
`/chat?resume=<id>` link) still opens under `worker`, so the embedded chat
sees that profile's MCP servers, model and skills. An explicit `?profile=`
in the URL always wins.

Pass `--isolated` to opt out and run a dedicated server scoped to that
profile (the pre-unification behavior — useful if you deliberately expose
different profiles' dashboards with different auth).

The **Chat** tab follows the switcher too: a scoped chat spawns its PTY
child with the selected profile's `HERMES_HOME`, so the conversation runs
with that profile's model, skills, memory, and session history. Switching
profiles starts a fresh terminal session.

Hub actions (skill install/update/uninstall, MCP install, toolset setup)
run with the target profile's own secret scope — its `.env` and configured
secret sources — not the dashboard process's environment; this includes
actions targeting the `default` profile from the machine dashboard.

What stays per-profile and is _not_ absorbed by the switcher: gateway
processes (manage them via `hermes -p <name> gateway …`), each profile's
session database, and cron schedulers (the Cron page already aggregates
across profiles with its own filter).

## Prerequisites [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#prerequisites "Direct link to Prerequisites")

FastAPI, Uvicorn, and the platform PTY helper are core Hermes dependencies.
The `web` extra adds exact constraints for the HTTP stack. The `pty` extra is
empty because its dependencies are already core. Standard PM setup includes
`web` through `all`.

If these dependencies are damaged, run `hermes pm repair` and restart Hermes.
For source setup, use the [PM developer workflow](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/package-management#developer-workflow).
Messaging and voice extras are separate requests, not implied by `all`.

When you run `hermes dashboard` without the dependencies, it will tell you what to install. If the frontend hasn't been built yet and `npm` is available, it builds automatically on first launch.

The Chat tab is part of every `hermes dashboard` launch — the embedded browser chat pane (running the TUI over PTY/WebSocket) is always available, with no extra flag required.

## Pages [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#pages "Direct link to Pages")

### Status [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#status "Direct link to Status")

The landing page shows a live overview of your installation:

- **Agent version** and release date
- **Gateway status** — running/stopped, PID, connected platforms and their state
- **Active sessions** — count of sessions active in the last 5 minutes
- **Recent sessions** — list of the 20 most recent sessions with model, message count, token usage, and a preview of the conversation

The status page auto-refreshes every 5 seconds.

#### Resource pressure banner [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#resource-pressure-banner "Direct link to Resource pressure banner")

When the host is running low on memory or disk, a banner appears at the top of
the dashboard (fed by the same status poll — no extra requests):

- **"Your agent is almost out of memory and may restart"** — system available
memory has dropped to _elevated_ (< 128 MiB or < 15%) or _critical_
(< 64 MiB or < 5%) levels, as sampled by the gateway's 30-second heartbeat.
- **"Your agent restarted unexpectedly, most likely because it ran out of**
**memory"** — the lifecycle ledger recorded an unclean exit under memory
pressure on the previous boot (a suspected OOM kill).
- **Disk warnings** — the volume holding `~/.hermes` is nearly full
( _elevated_ below 512 MB free, _critical_ below 256 MB free).

Only the most severe active warning shows at a time (disk critical > memory
critical > OOM restart > disk elevated > memory elevated). Dismissals are
scoped to the current gateway boot: dismissing a warning surfaces the next
active one, a gateway restart or an escalation (elevated → critical) re-opens
it, and a stale heartbeat renders nothing rather than a spurious alert.

On this page

The web dashboard is a browser-based UI for managing your Hermes Agent installation. Instead of editing YAML files or running CLI commands, you can configure settings, manage API keys, and monitor sessions from a clean web interface.

tip

Hosted-mode auth uses Nous Portal OAuth; if you also want the dashboard to talk to a real backend, `hermes setup --portal` wires up the model and tool gateway too. See [Nous Portal](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/nous-portal).

## Quick Start [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#quick-start "Direct link to Quick Start")

```bash
hermes dashboard
```

This starts a local web server and opens `http://127.0.0.1:9119` in your browser. The dashboard runs entirely on your machine — no data leaves localhost.

### Options [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#options "Direct link to Options")

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--port` | `9119` | Port to run the web server on |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address |
| `--no-open` | — | Don't auto-open the browser |
| `--insecure` | off | **Deprecated / no-op.** Formerly bypassed auth on a non-loopback bind; it no longer disables authentication — a public bind always requires an auth provider (password or OAuth) |
| `--isolated` | off | When launched from a named profile (`worker dashboard`), run a dedicated per-profile server instead of routing to the machine dashboard |

```bash
# Custom port

hermes dashboard --port 8080

# Bind to all interfaces (use with caution on shared networks)

hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0

# Start without opening browser

hermes dashboard --no-open
```

## Managing multiple profiles [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#managing-multiple-profiles "Direct link to Managing multiple profiles")

The dashboard is a **machine-level** management surface: one server manages
every [profile](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/profiles) on the machine. A profile switcher in the
sidebar (visible whenever more than one profile exists) decides which
profile the management pages read and write — Config, API Keys, Skills,
MCP, Models, and the Chat tab all follow it. While a profile other than
the dashboard's own is selected, an amber banner names the managed profile
so the write target is never ambiguous.

The selection lives in the URL (`?profile=<name>`), so deep links like
`http://127.0.0.1:9119/skills?profile=worker` land with the switcher
preselected and survive refresh.

Launching the dashboard from a profile alias routes to the machine
dashboard instead of starting a second server:

```bash
worker dashboard

# → already running: opens the browser at ?profile=worker

# → not running:     starts the machine dashboard with "worker" preselected
```

A dashboard started this way keeps `worker` as its fallback scope for the
whole server lifetime: a deep link that omits `?profile=` (for example a
`/chat?resume=<id>` link) still opens under `worker`, so the embedded chat
sees that profile's MCP servers, model and skills. An explicit `?profile=`
in the URL always wins.

Pass `--isolated` to opt out and run a dedicated server scoped to that
profile (the pre-unification behavior — useful if you deliberately expose
different profiles' dashboards with different auth).

The **Chat** tab follows the switcher too: a scoped chat spawns its PTY
child with the selected profile's `HERMES_HOME`, so the conversation runs
with that profile's model, skills, memory, and session history. Switching
profiles starts a fresh terminal session.

Hub actions (skill install/update/uninstall, MCP install, toolset setup)
run with the target profile's own secret scope — its `.env` and configured
secret sources — not the dashboard process's environment; this includes
actions targeting the `default` profile from the machine dashboard.

What stays per-profile and is _not_ absorbed by the switcher: gateway
processes (manage them via `hermes -p <name> gateway …`), each profile's
session database, and cron schedulers (the Cron page already aggregates
across profiles with its own filter).

## Prerequisites [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#prerequisites "Direct link to Prerequisites")

FastAPI, Uvicorn, and the platform PTY helper are core Hermes dependencies.
The `web` extra adds exact constraints for the HTTP stack. The `pty` extra is
empty because its dependencies are already core. Standard PM setup includes
`web` through `all`.

If these dependencies are damaged, run `hermes pm repair` and restart Hermes.
For source setup, use the [PM developer workflow](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/package-management#developer-workflow).
Messaging and voice extras are separate requests, not implied by `all`.

When you run `hermes dashboard` without the dependencies, it will tell you what to install. If the frontend hasn't been built yet and `npm` is available, it builds automatically on first launch.

The Chat tab is part of every `hermes dashboard` launch — the embedded browser chat pane (running the TUI over PTY/WebSocket) is always available, with no extra flag required.

## Pages [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#pages "Direct link to Pages")

### Status [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#status "Direct link to Status")

The landing page shows a live overview of your installation:

- **Agent version** and release date
- **Gateway status** — running/stopped, PID, connected platforms and their state
- **Active sessions** — count of sessions active in the last 5 minutes
- **Recent sessions** — list of the 20 most recent sessions with model, message count, token usage, and a preview of the conversation

The status page auto-refreshes every 5 seconds.

#### Resource pressure banner [​](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard\#resource-pressure-banner "Direct link to Resource pressure banner")

When the host is running low on memory or disk, a banner appears at the top of
the dashboard (fed by the same status poll — no extra requests):

- **"Your agent is almost out of memory and may restart"** — system available
memory has dropped to _elevated_ (< 128 MiB or < 15%) or _critical_
(< 64 MiB or < 5%) levels, as sampled by the gateway's 30-second heartbeat.
- **"Your agent restarted unexpectedly, most likely because it ran out of**
**memory"** — the lifecycle ledger recorded an unclean exit under memory
pressure on the previous boot (a suspected OOM kill).
- **Disk warnings** — the volume holding `~/.hermes` is nearly full
( _elevated_ below 512 MB free, _critical_ below 256 MB free).

Only the most severe active warning shows at a time (disk critical > memory
critical > OOM restart > disk elevated > memory elevated). Dismissals are
scoped to the current gateway boot: dismissing a warning surfaces the next
active one, a gateway restart or an escalation (elevated → critical) re-opens
it, and a stale heartbeat renders nothing rather than a spurious alert.
